title: Expected distribution
view: Two gender-neutral adults in the anatomical position, front view (patient's right on the image left): skeleton on the left, grey body on the right; right-sided block. Concept after NYSORA's block distribution figures (concept only).
teachingPoint: A fascia iliaca block reaches the femoral and lateral femoral cutaneous nerves: the anterior and lateral thigh, the knee, and the medial leg to the ankle; the hip joint, femur and knee in bone.
claims: Femoral nerve territory: anterior thigh, anterior knee, and medial leg to the medial ankle and foot via the saphenous branch (record anatomy: the spread reaches the femoral nerve; NYSORA: femoral nerve and its branches).
Lateral femoral cutaneous territory: lateral thigh to just above the knee (record anatomy; NYSORA).
Obturator spread is inconsistent (NYSORA: rarely) and is not shaded.
Right-sided block, patient's right on the image left (house laterality).
Colour key: teal = femoral nerve (with its saphenous branch), violet = lateral femoral cutaneous nerve; the key is shown under the image in the app, not on the plate (owner, 2026-10-15).

Bone: the femur (head, neck, shaft, condyles) and patella (femoral articular branches to the hip and knee), plus the saphenous periosteal territory: the anteromedial proximal tibia and the medial distal tibia with the medial malleolus. Not shaded: the pelvis, fibula, tibial mid-shaft and lateral tibia (sciatic territories). Owner, 2026-10-15: realistic coverage; sources: Lundblad et al. 2013 (saphenous innervation of the medial ankle, Local Reg Anesth 6:13), cadaveric saphenous periosteal branches 3.9-8.2 cm above the malleolus; NCT05728294 (proximal tibia femoral anteriorly, sciatic posteriorly).
